label: SharePoint
description: Bring files and folders from SharePoint sites into a project, with an app key an admin sets up once.
usage_notes: SharePoint files reach you only when the person imports them into the project with "Add files from SharePoint"; work on those project files. Don't call Microsoft Graph or SharePoint with this connection's key, and don't browse or download from SharePoint yourself. If a file the person mentions isn't in the project, ask them to import it.

form.title: Connect SharePoint
form.subtitle: Read the SharePoint sites an admin grants to an Entra app, and import their files into projects.

methods.label: App key (admin)
methods.description: An app registered in your Microsoft Entra with the Graph permission Sites.Selected. It reads only the sites an admin grants it.
methods.how_to:
## Set up the app key

An admin does this once. It needs a **Global Administrator** or **Privileged Role Administrator**: a SharePoint Administrator alone can't grant the consent or the site access.

1. In [Microsoft Entra → App registrations](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_RegisteredApps/ApplicationsListBlade), choose **New registration**. Name it, keep **Single tenant**, and register it.
2. On the app's **Overview**, copy the **Application (client) ID** and the **Directory (tenant) ID**.
3. Go to **API permissions → Add a permission → Microsoft Graph → Application permissions**, add `Sites.Selected`, then click **Grant admin consent**.
4. Go to **Certificates & secrets → Client secrets → New client secret**, pick an expiry, and copy the **Value** at once (it is shown only once).
5. Give the app read access to each site Cowork may use. In [Graph Explorer](https://developer.microsoft.com/graph/graph-explorer), signed in as an admin whose token holds `Sites.FullControl.All`:
   - `GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/{host}:/sites/{site}` and copy the `id`.
   - `POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/sites/{that id}/permissions` with
     `{"roles": ["read"], "grantedToIdentities": [{"application": {"id": "{client id}", "displayName": "{app name}"}}]}`.
   - Use the app's **client id** in the body, not the site id. A `201` means it worked.
6. Enter the tenant id, client id, client secret and site addresses here, one site per line.

## Notes

- With `Sites.Selected` the app reaches only the sites granted in step 5.
- Anyone who can use this connection sees what the app was granted, whatever their own SharePoint permissions.
